<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Keep Anthropic inline system reminders out of the leading prompt prefix when a template requires system-first ordering. Addresses #53393; refreshed against main `c5f8adc0` and the renderer resolution introduced in #58754.

## Claims

- Re-role inline system messages to user in place and merge adjacent user content only on the existing system-first fallback; preserve inline system roles for accepting templates.
- Retain current renderer and request-conversion APIs, and update the startup warning to describe user-role framing rather than a leading-system merge.

## Validation

- `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/entrypoints/anthropic/test_anthropic_messages_conversion.py -v` — **111 passed**.
- After the final warning-only update: the same file with `-k InlineSystem -q` — **15 passed**.
- The three fallback regressions fail against unmodified main production code and pass with this fix.
- Pre-commit on both changed files and `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD` — **passed**.
- No current-head model/serving evaluation ran here; CUDA cannot initialize. The production middleware measurements linked in this discussion support the transformation direction but did not execute this patch.

## Details

Hoisting each per-turn reminder into the leading system block changes the prompt prefix on every request. This preserves reminder text and its conversation position, but intentionally changes its role framing to user. Tool/reasoning-history compatibility still needs current-head model validation.

Duplicate/overlap check: #52978 uses trailing-system hoisting; #47681 changes a shared merge policy. Open Draft #58772 materially overlaps the goal but introduces a broader preserve/fold normalizer, tool-result folding, renderer probes and a CLI policy. This PR retains the narrower existing fallback and adds no normalization policy or CLI option. Maintainer guidance is requested on whether to take this small fix first or consolidate into #58772; no independent-scope claim is made. #58754 fixes template detection and does not remove the rejecting-template fallback.

Open since 2026-08-24. AI assistance was used for the refresh; signed-off, signed commits include Codex attribution. Human review and GPU/model validation remain required.

nodes.body: Hello @DarkLight1337 @robertgshaw2-redhat @aarnphm @NickLucche @AndreasKaratzas @mgoin, when you have a chance, could you please review this PR? It preserves prefix-cache behavior for inline system turns. Any feedback or guidance on the implementation and test coverage would be greatly appreciated. Thank you for your time!

Tested the same transformation (inline system -> user in place) in production on Qwen3.8-27B-FP8 / vLLM v0.28.0 with Claude Code 2.1.296, via a request-rewriting middleware rather than this patch. Second request of a session: prefix-cache hits 14,112/20,068 -> 18,816/20,083, TTFT 1.9 s -> 0.48 s. Over 7 days before the change the aggregate hit rate was 31% with mean TTFT 19.5 s. Setup and numbers in #53393.

The patch no longer applies on main after #58754 (`_should_merge_inline_system` and the renderer changes). Do you plan to rebase? Happy to help test.

Hi @mgoin @NickLucche @chaunceyjiang @aarnphm @AndreasKaratzas @DarkLight1337 @robertgshaw2-redhat, I merged main `c5f8adc0`, retained #58754's resolved-template detection/current renderer API, and updated the startup warning to describe the actual in-place user-role fallback. The description now records the current PR checklist, signed-off/AI attribution, tests and model-validation limits.

Validation: **111 conversion tests passed**, with **15 inline-system tests** rerun after the warning update; the three fallback regressions fail on main. The production middleware results reported by wndaasa support the direction but did not test this head.

Open since **August 24**, this still affects rejecting templates because main continues to hoist their per-turn reminders into the leading prefix. Draft **#58772 overlaps** and proposes broader normalization/tool-result handling; this PR keeps the narrower existing fallback. Could you please review the updated diff and advise whether to advance this small fix or consolidate into #58772? Current-head tool/reasoning/model validation is still needed. Thank you.

Tested the current head (8c25637) offline against captured Claude Code 2.1.296 traffic, rendered through the Qwen3.8-27B template.

Setup: `VLLM_USE_PRECOMPILED=1 uv pip install -e .` at 8c25637, Python 3.12. Two consecutive requests from one session (first user turn, then the same conversation after a tool call) converted with `to_chat_completion_request(merge_inline_system=True)` and rendered with `apply_chat_template` (tools included, `reasoning_effort="medium"`). `_detect_merge_inline_system` returns True for the stock Qwen3.8 template, so this exercises the fallback path.

- main (c5f8adc0): request 2 shares 15,430 of request 1's 19,841 tokens (77.8%). The divergence is inside the leading system block, where the per-turn `<total_tokens>` reminder gets appended.
- this PR: request 2 shares all 19,841 tokens (100%); request 1's rendered prompt is an exact prefix of request 2, and the reminder renders as a trailing `user` turn after the tool results (roles: system, user, assistant, tool, tool, user).
- `tests/entrypoints/anthropic/test_anthropic_messages_conversion.py`: 111 passed (15 inline-system cases).

This is conversion + rendering only, not a live run of this head against the model. The live numbers in #53393 came from the same transformation applied by a request-rewriting middleware in front of v0.28.0 (97.6% prefix-cache hit rate over 126 real requests, mean TTFT 0.83 s, versus 31% / 19.5 s before).

Thank you @wndaasa for testing `8c25637` with captured traffic and the Qwen3.8 template, and for rerunning the 111 tests. The shared-prefix improvement from 77.8% to 100%, with tools included, is useful validation of the fallback on this head.

I also appreciate your clearly separating the conversion/rendering test from the earlier middleware production measurements. Live model validation of this head, including tool/reasoning behavior, remains outstanding. Thanks again for taking the time to help test this!

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.

@@ -1003,6 +1003,78 @@ def test_inline_system_billing_header_mixed_with_content(self):
         assert result.messages[1]["content"] == "Real system content."
 
 
+class TestInlineSystemMessageMerge:
+    def test_inline_system_is_rerolled_and_merged_with_user_turns(self):
+        request = _make_request(
+            [
+                {"role": "user", "content": "Q"},
+                {"role": "system", "content": "LATESYS"},
+                {"role": "user", "content": "Q2"},
+            ]
+        )
+
+        result = _convert(request, merge_inline_system=True)
+
+        assert result.messages == [
+            {
+                "role": "user",
+                "content": [
+                    {"type": "text", "text": "Q"},
+                    {"type": "text", "text": "LATESYS"},
+                    {"type": "text", "text": "Q2"},
+                ],
+            }
+        ]
+
+    def test_inline_system_with_top_level_system_stays_after_prefix(self):
+        request = _make_request(
+            [
+                {"role": "user", "content": "Hello"},
+                {"role": "system", "content": "Be concise."},
+            ],
+            system="Top-level prompt.",
+        )
+
+        result = _convert(request, merge_inline_system=True)
+
+        assert result.messages == [
+            {"role": "system", "content": "Top-level prompt."},
+            {
+                "role": "user",
+                "content": [
+                    {"type": "text", "text": "Hello"},
+                    {"type": "text", "text": "Be concise."},
+                ],
+            },
+        ]
+
+    def test_inline_system_block_content_is_converted_to_user_text(self):
+        request = _make_request(
+            [
+                {"role": "user", "content": "Hello"},
+                {
+                    "role": "system",
+                    "content": [
+                        {"type": "text", "text": "Part one. "},
+                        {"type": "text", "text": "Part two."},
+                    ],
+                },
+            ]
+        )
+
+        result = _convert(request, merge_inline_system=True)
+
+        assert result.messages == [
+            {
+                "role": "user",
+                "content": [
+                    {"type": "text", "text": "Hello"},
+                    {"type": "text", "text": "Part one. Part two."},
+                ],
+            }
+        ]
+
+
